Adam Wyman joins Danny Jones for an episode billed as dark science, gathering four heavy subjects: death itself, DARPA's research programs, Anthony Fauci and the pandemic years, and nuclear war. The conversation treats secret and high-stakes research as one shadowy landscape worth mapping in a single pass.

Wyman moves between the topics as connected evidence of how governments study the extremes of life and death away from public view. Some of what he cites is documented program history; the connections he draws are his own. Jones keeps the tour moving at the pace of a late-night seminar. Listeners get a survey of the modern state's darkest laboratories as one researcher assembles them, with the seams between record and inference left for the audience to find.

Joe Rogan honors the genius of Bill Hicks in a segment from his show. Hicks was the dark, fierce comic who died young in 1994 and grew to myth after death. Rogan counts him as a hero of the stage.

Rogan tells what made Hicks great: rage at lies, love of truth, and jokes that cut like knives. He shares the bits that still get told in green rooms each night. He asks why the crowd found Hicks too late. Listeners new to the name get a fine first door. The library holds the segment as an archive record of the praise.
